VP010.R12A: Mop moves toward the foreground, with conspicuous bright raised splash/foam behind it aroundframe57 and broad smooth patches on the water.

VP010.R12B_native_text_value_off: Mop motion remains, but floor/wall brightness changes much more strongly from early frames and circular/ring-like patterns appear around the mop later. These differences do not show a reliably cleaner physical absorption process.
VP010.R12B_pretext_read: Main mop motion and bright water/splash-like regions remain close to normalR12B in the sampled frames; moving the query before native text does not visibly resolve the absorption/process issue.

VP027.caption: Hands shape a lump of clay-like bread dough into a smooth, round boule on a wooden table.
VP027.R10A: Hands and rounded dough remain clear but largely static in the sampled frames.
VP027.R12B: Hands perform visible repositioning/patting/shaping after the initial hold; the single dough mass remains recognizable and broadly rounded. No severe global grid or object disappearance seen in the earlierR11B case. This is a local positive process/visual observation relative to the mostlystaticR10A example, not proof of fullgoal success.
VP027.R12B_native_text_value_off: Hands press and deform the dough more strongly, while hands/dough remain recognizable and no global grid appears. The prompt specifically asks for a smooth round boule, so greater pressing or flattening is not by itself better compliance. The sampled views do not establish an unambiguous overall winner for this pair.
VP027.R12B_no_c: Hands and single dough mass remain recognizable; shaping occurs without C. A pronounced ghosted hand is visible around sampled frame45, whereas normal maintains clearer hands in those samples. This is a local possible consistency benefit, not full-suite evidence.

VP034.caption: A large, clear balloon is inflated with air, showing the internal pressure causing the balloon to stretch.
VP034.R10A: A clear rounded balloon persists, mostlystatic with slight position changes; sustained inflation/stretch is not convincing in the sampled frames.
VP034.R12B: Balloon remains recognizable and mostlyround while drifting up/down; a sustained increase in size consistent with the requested inflation is not clear. No severe global texture damage, but displacement is not evidence of inflation.
VP034.R12B_native_text_value_off: Similar upward/drifting balloon and progressively brighter/whiter appearance. Stable object plus drift does not by itself complete the requested pressure-driven stretching, even though AutoEval givesSA4/PC5.
VP034.R12B_no_c: Balloon remains round and drifts with minor apparent size changes, without convincing sustained requested inflation. The missing process persists without physics.

paired_interpretation: OnVP004/010 the new text interaction mitigates some corruption/appearance drift, yet these physicalprocesses remain weak. OnVP027 normal retains a rounded dough mass while showing shaping action; off gives larger pressing/deformation, which is not automatically better for the round-boule request. These case-specific observations must be combined with complete16/40 scores, pretext_read andno_c. Do not select an architecture or claim complete improvement from motion or a single control mean.
input_comparability: Same caption, seed, checkpoint for normal/off; same first-image pixels acrossR10A/R12A/R12B. Complete40 native input/noise sources and images also match originalR10A (matched_generation_inputs40.json).
pretext_visual_interpretation: On these two predeclared cases the changed query order alone does not remove the main failures. This does not determine the complete16 score effect or the benefit of retraining with pre-text queries; the completed control andno_c remain required.
no_c_interpretation: Normal16 versus noC improves PC+.125 (3wins/12ties/1loss), harms SA-.1875 (0wins/13ties/3losses), Joint5 versus6. Actual videos show native generation already supplies main motion; C may improve local hand consistency but does not repair missing process and can interfere with requested execution.
